research_question: Can a 3B Neural Compiler achieve cross-domain semantic grounding and multi-step planning through schema conditioning and depth curriculum, while maintaining TaskIR structural correctness?

capability_schema_coverage.spider: SEMANTIC_ONLY (table names, no full schema in corpus)

depth_curriculum.note: 7+ bucket has only 17 samples — oversampling at 5x gives max 85 effective

evaluation_protocol.tau3_external_dev: τ³ 2546 tasks (2048 protocol after Task 0 fix)
evaluation_protocol.agentboard: UNTouched holdout — not to be run until Phase 5C model frozen

prohibited: Label modification based on external benchmarks
Hyperparameter tuning based on external benchmark scores

selection.rules_frozen_before_supplements: (1) internal matched Valid>=97%; (2) BFCL Functional max; (3) tau3 Grounded Semantic Recall + Count Ratio
selection.deployment_protocol: inference MUST include capability schemas via build_capability_prompt (matched training protocol)
selection.rationale: gate: all four pass; BFCL functional S 18.19 highest; tau3 recall indistinguishable; internal opseq 94.11 also highest
selection.depth_reweighting_verdict: removed from mainline (negative factor: hurts internal opseq -4.78pp, tau3 parse -12pp, BFCL functional -1.04pp)

key_findings: Schema conditioning: first positive evidence for cross-domain semantic grounding (BFCL functional +1.36pp), requires schema at training AND inference
Depth curriculum: length is trainable (+0.65) but correctness is not (tau3 recall flat 0.55-0.66%)
EXEC_ACTION boundary: tau3 96% refs lower to EXEC_ACTION, models emit ~0 despite 1649 training examples - conditional mapping fails to transfer; isomorphic to BFCL multi_turn failure
Internal OpSeq collapse in bare-prompt eval was train/eval mismatch, not capability loss (94.11/89.82 recovered under matched prompts)
